class.name: PlayFabPartyConfig
class.brief_description: Configuration for [PlayFabParty] initialization and network create/join.
class.description: Optional configuration for [method PlayFabParty.initialize_async], [method PlayFabParty.create_and_join_network_async], [method PlayFabParty.join_network_async], and [method PlayFabPartyChat.create_local_chat_control_async]. Pass audio fields to the latter before joining a network; joins reuse existing chat controls. Chat-related fields are addon policy flags, not native Party network settings.

members.member: Maximum number of players permitted in the Party network.

Direct peer connectivity policy bitmask. See [enum PlayFabParty.DirectPeerConnectivity]. Defaults to [constant PlayFabParty.DIRECT_PEER_CONNECTIVITY_NONE] (all traffic relayed through PlayFab Party). Platform-type and entity-login-provider flags must be combined; for the common "any platform + any login provider" preset use [constant PlayFabParty.DIRECT_PEER_CONNECTIVITY_ANY]. Invalid combinations cause [method PlayFabParty.create_and_join_network_async] to fail synchronously with code [code]party_invalid_options[/code].
Optional invitation id; the addon generates one if empty.
Whether the addon should create and connect a voice chat control.
Whether the addon should enable text chat on the chat control.

Whether the addon should enable speech-to-text transcription on the chat control. When [code]true[/code] the addon calls [code]SetTranscriptionOptions[/code] on the local chat control for the local user plus all remote controls, in both matching and non-matching languages, so [signal PlayFabPartyChat.transcription_received] fires.

Whether the addon should enable translation on the chat control. Translation is receiver-side in PlayFab Party: when [code]true[/code] the addon asks Party to translate incoming text chat (and, when [member enable_transcription] is also set, incoming transcriptions) into this control's language, surfaced as [member PlayFabPartyChatMessage.translated_text].

Audio input (microphone) device id bound on the local chat control. Empty uses [member audio_device_default_mode]. A non-empty id always selects [code]Manual[/code], overriding the default mode for input only. Binding does not guarantee voice flow: chat permissions and audio subsystem initialization must also succeed.

Audio output (speaker) device id bound on the local chat control. Empty uses [member audio_device_default_mode]. A non-empty id always selects [code]Manual[/code], overriding the default mode for output only. Binding does not guarantee voice flow: chat permissions and audio subsystem initialization must also succeed.

Default selection policy shared by empty [member audio_input] and [member audio_output]. [constant AUDIO_DEVICE_DEFAULT_AUTO] preserves compile-target behavior; shared desktop-built DLLs should explicitly select [constant AUDIO_DEVICE_DEFAULT_SYSTEM] on PC or [constant AUDIO_DEVICE_DEFAULT_PLATFORM_USER] on Xbox. Platform-user selection resolves the owning Xbox-backed [PlayFabUser]'s decimal XUID internally, independently of compile target, and retains context for the chat control's lifetime. If a direction needs platform-user selection and identity cannot be resolved, creation fails with [code]party_chat_control_create_failed[/code]; no identity is required when both device ids are explicit. Unsupported modes fail with [code]party_invalid_options[/code], including when both ids are explicit. Configuration is snapshotted for async creation. An existing control is reused without reconfiguration; destroy and recreate it to change devices or mode.

BCP-47 language code applied to the local chat control at creation. Empty keeps the Party default (the platform's language). This is the language used for outgoing text chat and voice transcription, and the target language for receiver-side translation.

constants.constant: Legacy selection: [code]PlatformUserDefault[/code] for [code]_GAMING_XBOX[/code] builds, otherwise [code]SystemDefault[/code]. This is not runtime OS detection.
Use [code]SystemDefault[/code] with null context for empty device ids.
Use [code]PlatformUserDefault[/code] with the owner's resolved decimal XUID for empty device ids, including in desktop builds. Requires an Xbox-backed owner when either id is empty.
